items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google WASHINGTON, DC — The Washington Capitals allowed one of their more questionable goals so far this season against the New Jersey Devils on Saturday night, but the goal came on a play fans in DC thought should be called back. During a first-period power play for New Jersey, former Cap Connor Brown tied the game with what the NHL ruled was not a distinct kicking motion. With Brown at the netfront, Devils winger Jesper Bratt ferried the puck right to his skates, which sent the puck into the back of the net. Capitals fans were in uproar over the goal at Capital One Arena, and the NHL’s Situation Room deemed it borderline enough to warrant a video review. Ultimately, however, the goal stood. The guiding principle in this case is NHL Rule 37.4: Distinct Kicking Motion , which defines what counts as an illegal kick. Pucks are allowed to deflect off of skates and into the net, but a player who beats the goalie with a “distinct kicking motion” will have his goal overturned. After the video review, the Situation Room released a statement on their findings: Video review supported the Referee’s call on the ice that the puck deflected off Connor Brown’s skate and entered the net in a legal fashion. Rule 37.4 states, in part, “a puck that deflects into the net off an attacking Player’s skate who does not use a ‘distinct kicking motion’ shall be ruled a GOAL. A puck that is directed into the net by an attacking Players’ skate shall also be ruled a GOAL, as long as no ‘distinct kicking motion’ is evident.” Brown appeared to move his foot forward as the puck hit it, contributing to the eventual goal, but the NHL determined that his actions did not go far enough to break the rule. items.summary: The Maple Leafs aren’t rolling over, but they are most certainly rolling downhill. Luke Fox has the story after the team wrapped up a winless six-game homestand.
items.body: TORONTO — Difficult. Frustrating. Hard. Disappointing. Sucks. These are five of the adjectives the Toronto Maple Leafs used to describe a homestand in which they faced six strong opponents and failed to secure so much as a single point in the standings. After dropping a 1-0 nailbiter to the mighty Edmonton Oilers Saturday, the Maple Leafs’ home regulation losing skid now marks their longest home drought in 41 years. Even wilder: These Leafs became just the second team in NHL history to finish a home stand of six or more games with zero points. They join the 1970-71 L.A. Kings, who went on to miss the playoffs. If Toronto, a team still intending to make the dance, suffers a similar fate, we will look back at these two dreary November weeks as the fortnight that knocked it out, right? No team in the Atlantic Division has played more games than Toronto’s 22, and no team in the Atlantic has amassed fewer points (18). The Leafs aren’t rolling over, but they are most certainly rolling downhill. “We gave one hell of an effort. items.body: City’s second team, Abel, made debut against Montreal Maroons; play Canadiens Monday The arrival of the New York Rangers was one of the grandest events on the city’s 1926 social calendar. Given the choices for the top-hat and formal-gown set in the metropolis a century ago, that’s saying something. It was almost sidebar news that the Rangers, under coach Lester Patrick playing their first game in franchise history on Nov. 16, 1926, would defeat the Eddie Gerard -coached defending Stanley Cup-champion Montreal Maroons 1-0. Bill Cook , assisted by his brother, Fred (better known as Bun), scored the night’s only goal, bouncing a shot off the ear of Maroons goalie Clint Benedict at 18:37 of the second period. At the other end of Madison Square Garden ice, superb Hal Winkler was unbeatable in the Rangers net, stopping 48 shots to the 43 turned aside by Benedict. From left: Bill Cook, Frank Boucher and Fred “Bun” Cook were nicknamed as the A Line or Bread Line with the New York Rangers in the 1920s and 1930s. This undated photo was taken at Madison Square Garden in New York. The game featured another historical note: it included the participation of the Rangers’ Clarence “Taffy” Abel , by many reports the first player of Indigenous heritage to play in the NHL. Given the record keeping and social pressures of the time, it is impossible for the NHL to verify whether any indigenous players preceded Abel in the League. Undoubtedly, he was among the earliest. The bruising defenseman from Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan, was born to a Caucasian father and a mother who was Ojibwe, a member of the Chippewa First Nation. items.body: Veteran goalie receives silver stick to commemorate career achievement The Los Angeles Kings continued the celebration of Darcy Kuemper on Saturday. The team honored the veteran goalie reaching the 500 NHL games played milestone with a special pregame ceremony before their game against the Calgary Flames at Crypto.com Arena. Kuemper’s wife, Sydney, sons, Caden and Barrett, parents Brent and Sharon, and siblings, Brendan and Nicole, joined him on the ice for the festivities. A tribute video featuring highlights throughout the veteran goalie’s 15 NHL seasons and special video messages from his Kings teammates aired on the arena video board. 5️⃣0️⃣0️⃣ games! Congratulations, Darcy! pic.twitter.com/vkcqgMtgbD Kings president Luc Robitaille presented Kuemper with the commemorative silver stick. His sons also received miniature versions of the silver goalie sticks. The team’s goalie coach Mike Buckley presented the veteran goalie with a Tiffany crystal on behalf of the NHL. Kuemper’s teammates gifted him a Rolex watch, a custom goalie mask featuring career highlights, a custom holographic trading card and trip for his family to a Colorado Springs resort. On Thursday, Kuemper played in his 500 th NHL game in a matchup against the New York Islanders. His teammates wore custom T-shirts honoring his achievement. The veteran goalie is in his third straight season with the Kings and played 19 games for the team during the 2017-2018 season. He played five seasons for the Minnesota Wild (2012-17), four seasons with the Arizona Coyotes (2018-21), two seasons with the Washington Capitals (2022-24) and one season with the Colorado Avalanche (2021-22). Kuemper helped the Avalanche to a Stanley Cup championship in 2022.

items.summary: The Canadiens had a good loss to the Avalanche days after a bad win over the Bruins. Things have a way of evening out over an 84-game season, and sometimes it happens even quicker than expected, writes Eric Engels.
items.body: MONTREAL— This game against the Colorado Avalanche wasn’t a bad one for the Montreal Canadiens . Not like the one they won 5-2 against the Boston Bruins right before it. But the Canadiens lost 4-1 Saturday because things have a way of evening out over an 84-game season, and sometimes it happens even quicker than expected. This time, it happened within just 48 hours, and it’s good the Canadiens had that in perspective afterwards. It came into this game on a 12-game point streak, at 9-0-3, and it was honest in its assessment of why it ended. Juraj Slafkovsky was right when he said execution was lacking. And Captain Nick Suzuki , who scored the team’s only goal in the game, correctly cited a lack of discipline as an impediment to positive momentum when the Canadiens needed it most — while they trailed by two goals in the third period. But penalties to Josh Anderson and Adam Engstrom aside, the process was where it needed to be to give the Canadiens a chance, and it was specifically geared towards correcting what should’ve taken a chance away from them against the Bruins on Thursday. They didn’t succeed on the scoreboard, but at least they succeeded in that. “I think we were tighter through the neutral zone,” said Suzuki. “Obviously they’re a good rush team, they’re going to create some chances, like their first goal. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dallas Stars forward Jamie Benn became the latest player to reach 1,000 career NHL regular-season points, scoring in the second period on Saturday night in a 2-0 win over the Buffalo Sabres . The 37-year-old got the rebound on a loose puck in front of the net before sliding a shot over the goal line to open the scoring late in the second period, marking the 418th regular-season goal of his career. In his 18th NHL season, all of Benn’s points have come with the Stars , ranking him second in franchise history—dating back to the team’s days as the Minnesota North Stars— for points, behind Mike Modano’s 1,359 career points. The crowd at the American Airlines Center exploded in celebration after the goal, and the Stars’ bench emptied to congratulate the franchise legend, who now boasts 418 goals and 582 assists for 1,000 career points in 1,272 regular-season games. Drafted in the fifth round of the 2007 NHL Draft, Benn made the Stars’ opening night roster in 2009-10 and netted his first point with an assist in just his second game. In 2014-15, he reached his peak scoring point, posting 35 goals and 52 assists for 87 points to win the Art Ross Trophy. He elevated his goal-scoring touch the season after, finding the back of the net 41 times in the 2015-16 campaign. In addition to his regular-season totals, Benn has 28 goals and 52 assists for 80 points in 126 Stanley Cup Playoff games, reaching the final in the 2019-20 season in the COVID-19 bubble playoffs before falling to the Tampa Bay Lightning . items.summary: Nathan MacKinnon will be out one month, and Cale Makar will be sidelined two weeks, Colorado Avalanche coach Jared Bednar announced before their 4-1 win against the Montreal Canadiens on Saturday.
items.body: Nathan MacKinnon will be out one month, and Cale Makar will be sidelined two weeks, Colorado Avalanche coach Jared Bednar announced before their 4-1 win against the Montreal Canadiens on Saturday. Each sustained a lower-body injury in the second period of a 4-3 overtime loss to the Ottawa Senators on Thursday. MacKinnon's last shift came with 8:15 remaining in the second. The center grabbed his right side after attempting a reverse hit on Senators defenseman Artem Zub and stayed on the bench for a few minutes before heading down the tunnel. Makar took a shift at 10:44 of the second that lasted only four seconds before heading to the locker room. The defenseman briefly returned for a 23-second shift that ended with 5:20 remaining, but stayed on the bench for the rest of the period. The injury came four days after he left practice on Nov. 8 for precautionary reasons. "When I think about those two guys, it's like every matchup, they take it on, now someone else has to be able to step up and do that," Bednar said. "And then you are losing the depth down the lineup as you kind of do that because everyone is elevated." MacKinnon leads Colorado and is tied for fifth in the NHL with 30 points (10 goals, 20 assists) in 20 games; Makar is third on the Avalanche and tied for third among NHL defensemen with 23 points (five goals, 18 assists) in 19 games. "Probably the most important is the 5-on-5 offense that they create," Bednar said. "We can be playing an OK game, chances equal, tight game, and those guys, like the top players do, will find a way to make a play that's a difference-maker for you. Whether it's Cale or 'Mac,' or both of them combined, they generally win us a lot of hockey games because of that. So with out that, the rest of the game has to tighten up and get better.

items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that San Jose’s Will Smith preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to his goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 19:04 (0:56 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.summary: Dallas captain Jamie Benn scored a second-period goal during Saturday night’s game against the Buffalo Sabres for his 1,000th career NHL point, all with the Stars.
items.body: DALLAS — Dallas captain Jamie Benn scored a second-period goal during Saturday night’s game against the Buffalo Sabres for his 1,000th career NHL point, all with the Stars. Benn, 37, and in his 18th NHL season, is second to Hall of Famer Mike Modano (1,359) in career points for the franchise that began as the Minnesota North Stars in 1967 and moved to Texas in 1993. The Stars’ bench emptied to celebrate the moment when the longest-tenured captain in Stars history snapped a scoreless tie with his goal. Benn — a native of Victoria, British Columbia — was drafted in the fifth round in 2007 and made the Stars’ opening night roster in 2009, recording his first league point on an assist in his second game. He won the league’s 2014-15 Art Ross Trophy for leading the NHL with 87 points (35 goals, 52 assists). He scored a career-high 41 goals the following season, when he was selected for the second of his two All-Star teams. Benn’s 1,272 career regular-season games played are the most of any Stars skater since the team relocated to Dallas and ranks second in franchise history behind Modano’s 1,459. Benn missed the first 20 games last season when he had surgery for a collapsed lung on the eve of the opener. He was re-signed to a one-year contract in July.

items.summary: The Ontario native continued his insane start to the 2026-27 season with a point on Saturday in Toronto.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images One of the most exciting players in the game continues his incredible start to the 2026-27 season. Thanks to an assist on Evan Bouchard’s goal in the second period on Saturday night against the Toronto Maple Leafs , Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid extended his point streak to 21 games, a new career best. With that point, No. 97 also became the first player to hit the 50-point mark this year, with his point streak beginning at the start of the campaign. The 29-year-old has been scoring at a torrid pace thus far. While he has just 11 goals, his 39 assists and 50 points rank him far ahead of the rest of the league. In fact, McDavid broke Wayne Gretzky’s record for fewest games to reach 30 helpers in a season. While there is a lot of hockey to be played this season, the Richmond Hill, Ont. native is on pace to become the first player to reach 200 points in a single season since Gretzky scored a record 215 points during the 1985-86 season. The last time McDavid even reached 20 straight games with a point came…last year. The former No. 1 pick reached the mark from December to early January, notching 46 points during that time. While McDavid’s 21-game point streak is certainly impressive, it’s far from the best point streak in NHL history. In fact, he’s only tied for the 24th-longest point streak with legends Dave Taylor, Adam Oates, and Bobby Hull. All are far behind the longest point streak in league history, which came from The Great One himself, who posted points in 51 consecutive games to start the 1983-84 season, posting a ridiculous 153 points over that span. items.title: Senators looking to find fresh start for Andre Burakovsky
items.body: The Ottawa Senators and one of their veteran wingers appear to be heading for a mutual split. The Senators are out there looking to find a fresh start for André Burakovsky, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported during Saturday Night Hockey . Burakovsky has skated in just eight games for the Senators and has zero points after he was traded to Ottawa from the Chicago Blackhawks for a sixth-round pick in the off-season. Friedman added that he thinks the Senators will add to their roster at some point this season, but that he couldn't say if a potential Burakovsky move would be part of something bigger or if they will simply move him to create more opportunity for them to add. After sustaining a lower-body injury in a game against the Los Angeles Kings on Oct. 30, the most recent update on Burakovsky from Senators coach Travis Green was that he would be out for three to four weeks. The 31-year-old had 33 points (11 goals, 22 assists) in 75 games for the Blackhawks last season but has averaged just 64 games per campaign throughout his career. With zero points, the two-time 20-goal scorer is on pace for well below that level of production this season. However, it isn't just the Senators who are allegedly displeased with the union. The situation hasn't worked out well for everyone involved: the team and the player, according to Friedman's report.

items.body: FLA@STL: Keith Tkachuk kicks off the Blues vs Panthers with ceremonial puck-drop It was a full circle moment for the Tkachuk family on Saturday. The St. Louis Blues honored Keith Tkachuk for his 2026 Hockey Hall of Fame induction earlier this week before their game against the Florida Panthers at Enterprise Center. Tkachuk’s two sons, Panthers forwards Matthew Tkachuk and Brady Tkachuk , joined the retired forward at center ice for the ceremonial puck drop alongside Blues captain Robert Thomas . On a Saturday night with so many friends and family that are going to be here and my dad’s celebration. It really is an incredible night for us two and our family.” During player arrivals, Thomas sported Tkachuk’s No.7 Blues jersey. He lived with the Tkachuk family during his rookie season in 2019. Tkachuk played nine of his 18 NHL seasons with the Blues and retired with the team after the 2009-10 season. He also played six seasons for the Winnipeg Jets, who drafted him with the No. 19 pick in 1990 NHL Draft, and five seasons with the Phoenix Coyotes. In 1,201 career games, the retired forward recorded 1,065 points (538 goals, 527 assists). He is one of 50 NHL players to record 500 goals in their career and was the 41 st player to achieve the accomplishment.

items.body: Connor McDavid 's first point on Saturday against the Toronto Maple Leafs was a big one. The Edmonton Oilers captain set up Evan Bouchard for a goal late in the second to help the visitors take a 1-0 lead. Not only did it put him at 50 points for the 2026-27 campaign, but it also set his personal point-streak record, as he's now collected at least one point in all 21 games this season. McDavid has had two point streaks of 20 games previously in his career, but wasn't able to hit the 21-game mark until Saturday. If you're wondering how far McDavid has to go before he has a shot at the NHL record, it's a lot. Wayne Gretzky holds the NHL record for the longest point streak at 51 games, which he set in the 1983-84 season with the Oilers. Gretzky piled up a ridiculous 61 goals and 92 assists over the 51-game streak, and went on to finish the season with 205 points. McDavid, now at 11 goals and 39 assists over his 21-game tear, entered Saturday's game on pace for 206 points. Only Gretzky has ever surpassed the 200-point mark, a feat he accomplished four times over his career.

Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Pittsburgh’s Egor Chinakhov preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to Tommy Novak ’s goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 13:22 (6:38 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.summary: Scheifele passed Dale Hawerchuk as the Jets’ all-time franchise leader in points after he recorded his 930th on Saturday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Mark Scheifele has carved his name in the Winnipeg Jets’ record books. The forward earned his 930th point to become the Jets’ franchise leader in points after he scored against the Chicago Blackhawks Saturday afternoon. Scheifele passed Dale Hawerchuk, who recorded 929 points in his nine seasons with Winnipeg between 1981-82 and 1989-90. Scheifele finished the game with a goal and three assists for four points. The Jets would come back from a 4-0 deficit to win 5-4 in a shootout. The 33-year-old center now has seven goals and 19 assists for 26 points in 21 games this season. Now in his 16th NHL season, Scheifele, a native of Kitchener, Ont., has 379 goals and 554 assists for 933 points in 982 career regular-season games. He also has 26 goals and 23 assists for 49 points in 53 career Stanley Cup Playoff games. In October 2025, Scheifele passed Blake Wheeler as the all-time points leader in the second iteration of the Winnipeg Jets . Before the start of the 2026-27 season, the NHL announced they would consolidate the two versions of the club , which means the statistical achievements of both eras would be recorded together. The “new” Jets, or Jets 2.0, were originally known as the Atlanta Thrashers and played in the capital of Georgia between 1999 and 2011. It was bought by True North Sports & Entertainment, who relocated the team to Winnipeg. Once the second version of the Jets became official, the team selected Scheifele with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2011 NHL Entry Draft, becoming the first-ever player selected by Winnipeg 2.0.

Scheifele is now at 930 career points — all with Winnipeg — surpassing the Dale Hawerchuk's mark of 929 set with the first version of the franchise. The milestone comes after the NHL announced this summer that statistics from both versions of the Winnipeg Jets are now merged, something made possible after the Arizona Coyotes went dormant in 2024. Scheifele was the first-ever draft pick by the new Jets franchise after moving to Winnipeg from Atlanta in 2011. Since then, he has been a consistent offensive star over his 14 seasons, including scoring a career-high 103 points last season. This season, he had 22 points in 20 games entering action Saturday. Before being drafted by the Jets, Scheifele played under Hawerchuk when the Jets legend coached the OHL's Barrie Colts. Hawerchuk played nine of the 16 seasons in his Hall of Fame career with the Jets from 1981 to 1990. He died of cancer in 2020 at age 57.

items.title: Chris Kreider Out Six To Eight Weeks
items.summary: Montreal Canadiens winger Chris Kreider will miss the next six to eight weeks with a lower-body injury.
items.body: Register Login Chris Kreider Out Six To Eight Weeks By Brian La Rose | at November 14, 2026 2:15 pm The Canadiens will find themselves without a veteran winger for a while. The team announced ( Twitter link ) that Chris Kreider will miss approximately six to eight weeks due to a lower-body injury. The injury was sustained in the third period of Thursday’s victory in Boston following a collision with Michael Eyssimont . Kreider stayed down for a few seconds and was eventually able to hobble off largely under his own power but was unable to put any weight on his left leg. Kreider is in his first season with Montreal after joining them as a free agent a little before training camp. He reached an agreement on a mutual contract termination with Anaheim, allowing him to hit the open market where he inked a one-year, $2.15MM deal with another $3.25MM in potential performance bonuses. The 35-year-old has played in 19 games this season, meaning he has already hit $2MM of his bonus, that coming at the 10-game mark. He has three goals and six assists in those contests despite a pretty big drop in ice time; after logging over 17 minutes per night last season, Kreider is at just 13:21 this year. The rest of his bonuses are tied to goal production with the first payout coming at 10 goals, then at 20, 30, and 40. It’s safe to say at this point that the last two aren’t going to happen while even reaching 20 tallies will be tricky. Montreal was already carrying two extra forwards on its active roster so it’s unlikely that they will turn to a recall from AHL Laval. For tonight’s game against Colorado, rookie Florian Xhekaj will take Kreider’s spot in the lineup in what will be just his second game in November.

items.body: Register Login Penguins Assign Ilya Solovyov To AHL By Brian La Rose | at November 14, 2026 12:50 pm The Penguins have made a roster move in advance of their game tonight against Ottawa. The team announced ( Twitter link ) that they’ve assigned blueliner Ilya Solovyov to AHL Wilkes-Barre/Scranton. The 26-year-old is in his first full season with Pittsburgh’s organization after being acquired back in January. However, while Solovyov was a full-timer on the NHL roster last season, that hasn’t been the case this year, as he cleared waivers last month and spent a bit of time in the minors. Players who have cleared waivers can be on an NHL roster for 10 games or 30 days (whichever is reached first) before needing to clear again. Solovyov was only a handful of days away from the 30-day mark so by sending him down now, they avoid needing to run him through the waiver wire once again. items.title: Injured Avalanche stars MacKinnon, Makar to miss weeks
items.body: It's a double-whammy of injury trouble for the Colorado Avalanche . Both Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar will miss weeks, head coach Jared Bednar told reporters , beginning with Colorado's Saturday Night Hockey tilt against the Montreal Canadiens (Sportsnet, Sportsnet+, 7 p.m. ET / 5 p.m. PCT). MacKinnon is out at least one month, while Makar will miss approximately two weeks, per Bednar, who does not appear to have revealed the exact nature of the injuries. The Avalanche stars suffered injuries moments apart from each other during Thursday's 3-2 loss to the Ottawa Senators. MacKinnon sustained the injury after Senators defenceman Artem Zub cross-checked him in the hip area. Makar then left when he appeared to hurt his right leg after stopping to control the puck in the offensive zone. They had both been enjoying typically strong seasons, as MacKinnon has 10 goals and 20 assists through 20 games while Makar was at five goals and 23 points. items.title: Stars Make Three Roster Moves
items.summary: The Dallas Stars have recalled defenseman Kyle Burroughs from AHL Texas and made two other roster moves on the back end as well.
items.body: Register Login Stars Make Three Roster Moves By Brian La Rose | at November 14, 2026 10:37 am The Stars have made a trio of roster moves heading into their game tonight against Buffalo. The team announced ( Twitter link ) that they have recalled defenseman Kyle Burroughs from AHL Texas. To make room on the roster, blueliner Lian Bichsel was placed on IR. To create the cap room needed for the recall, defenseman Kyle Capobianco was placed on LTIR. Burroughs is in his first season with Dallas after signing a one-year, two-way deal back in July. The 31-year-old has played exclusively with Texas so far, picking up five assists and 10 penalty minutes through 15 contests so far. Burroughs does have a fair bit of NHL experience under his belt, however. He was a full-timer on an NHL roster as recently as two years ago, when he had a full-time seventh role with Los Angeles, a year after playing in a career-high 73 games in San Jose. Overall, Burroughs has 22 points, 293 blocks, and 572 hits in 201 career NHL appearances. It wouldn’t be shocking to see Burroughs be in the seventh role while up with Dallas. That said, he could alternate with youngster Trey Taylor depending on the matchup as well. Bichsel’s IR placement should come as no surprise given that he received a week-to-week designation on Friday due to a lower-body injury. Meanwhile, Capobianco was placed on IR retroactive to October 27th, meaning he has already missed more than half of the 10-game, 24-day minimum absence for a player to be LTIR-eligible. The initial timeline was that he’d miss around four weeks with his leg injury so he may still be on track to return at the end of the month.

items.summary: Chris Kreider has three goals and nine points in 19 games with Montreal in 2026-27.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Montreal Canadiens announced Saturday that forward Chris Kreider will be out for approximately six-to-eight weeks with a lower-body injury. The 35-year-old winger suffered the injury after Boston Bruins’ forward Michael Eyssimont slid into him during their game Thursday. Kreider went straight to the dressing room and did not return. In 19 games, Kreider has three goals and six assists for nine points. He signed a one-year, $2.15-million deal with Montreal in September after the Anaheim Ducks terminated his contract. In 2025-26, Kreider had 22 goals and 28 assists for 50 points in 75 games with the Ducks. He finished second on the team with eight power-play goals and reached the 20-goal mark for the eighth straight season. Through 15 NHL seasons, Kreider, a native of Boxford, Mass., has 351 goals and 290 assists for 641 points in 977 career regular-season games with the Canadiens, Ducks and New York Rangers . items.body: The Columbus Blue Jackets will be without their bench boss on Saturday. Coach Rick Bowness will miss his second straight game when his team hosts the Philadelphia Flyers, general manager Don Waddell told reporters . Bowness also missed Thursday's 3-1 loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning and was not present for practice on Friday or Saturday's morning skate. items.body: The Montreal Canadiens will be down a forward for the next while. Chris Kreider is expected to miss six to eight weeks with a lower-body injury the team announced on Saturday. In Thursday night's win against the Boston Bruins, Kreider was sent down the tunnel with less than 14 minutes remaining in the third period after Bruins forward Michael Eyssimont fell at the centre-ice line and slid into the veteran's knee. Edmonton Oilers center Connor McDavid will put his 20-game season-opening point streak on the line in his hometown for Hockey Night in Canada showdown against the slumping Toronto Maple Leafs at Scotiabank Arena (7 p.m. ET; SNO, SNW, SNP, NHLN). McDavid is the fourth different player in NHL history with at least one point in each of the first 20 games of a season. Wayne Gretzky did it three times, including his record-51-game point streak to open the 1983-84 season. Mats Sundin (30 games, 1992-93) and Dany Heatley (22 games, 2005-06) are the others. McDavid leads the League with 49 points (11 goals, 38 assists). If he extends his point streak he will also become the fifth different player in NHL history to have 50 points by the 21st game of the season, joining Gretzky (three times), Mario Lemieux (three times), Bernie Nicholls and Mike Bossy . No one has done it since Lemieux in 1995-96. The Oilers (14-3-3) have won three straight, with points in 11 of 13 (9-2-2). It's the opposite for center Auston Matthews and the Maple Leafs (8-11-2), who have lost five straight games, all at home, by a combined 22-9. Salvaging a win in the finale of a six-game homestand would at least stop the bleeding. Toronto won 7-2 at Edmonton on Oct. 24, when forward William Nylander scored two goals. He has three in eight games since. This will also be Oilers coach Mike Babcock's first game in Toronto since being fired as Maple Leafs coach on Nov. 20, 2019.

items.body: Register Login Hurricanes Activate Jordan Staal, Place Mike Reilly On Waivers By Ryan Long | at November 14, 2026 9:34 am The Hurricanes will have their captain back for the second game of their Global Series set in Helsinki. Carolina announced it has activated Jordan Staal from injured reserve ahead of today’s game against the Kraken. To make room on the roster, the club placed defenseman Mike Reilly on waivers. Staal, 38, has missed the past 14 games after partially tearing his calf in warmups before an October 11 win in Philadelphia. Head coach Rod Brind’Amour originally said he’d be out one to two months, and Staal is back about a month later. He practiced with the team twice in Finland this week and worked on special teams Friday. He’s projected to center the third line between Seth Jarvis and Jordan Martinook . Staal had no points in six games before the injury, though he won 55.6% of his faceoffs and recorded 19 hits. He’s coming off a playoff run that ended with the Conn Smythe Trophy, eight goals and 12 points in 19 games, with six of those goals coming in the Final against Vegas. Reilly, 33, re-signed with Carolina in September on a one-year, two-way deal worth $850K in the NHL and $450K in the AHL. He came into the lineup after the Hurricanes lost their first two games, playing on the third pair with Shayne Gostisbehere and picking up two assists. He has been a frequent healthy scratch since mid-October. The 12-year veteran played 42 games for Carolina last season, with one goal, nine points and a plus-11 rating, and added two assists in two games during the Cup run. If he clears, the Hurricanes will send him to AHL Chicago.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Bolte-Imagn Images The Carolina Hurricanes will soon get their captain back. The team announced Saturday that forward Jordan Staal has been activated off injured reserve and he will be available to play against the Seattle Kraken Saturday in Finland. Staal, 38, has been out of the lineup since he suffered a tear in his calf during the pregame warmups ahead of Carolina’s game against the Philadelphia Flyers Oct. 10. The six-foot-four center was pointless through his first six games this season but is coming up a 2025-26 campaign that saw him score 20 goals and add 16 assists for 36 points in 75 games. Staal led the Hurricanes to their second Stanley Cup championship in franchise history as he scored eight goals and added four assists for 12 points. He was awarded the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP. He signed a one-year contract extension in the offseason that will keep him with the team through the 2027-28 season. He has served as Carolina’s fulltime captain since 2019-20 after two seasons as co-captain with Justin Faulk. Staal, taken No. 2 overall by the Pittsburgh Penguins in the 2006 NHL Entry Draft, has 318 goals and 429 assists for 747 points in 1,409 career regular-season games with the Hurricanes and Penguins. He also has 46 goals and 39 assists for 85 points in 181 career playoff games. Along with his championship in 2026, Staal helped Pittsburgh win the Stanley Cup in 2009 and was part of their run to the Final in 2008.

Because the payoff wasn’t a rec game in their municipal rink. items.body: Register Login Kraken Activate Ryan Lindgren, Reassign Logan Morrison By Ryan Long | at November 14, 2026 8:03 am The Seattle Kraken have activated defenseman Ryan Lindgren from injured reserve, the team announced this morning. To make room on the roster, forward Logan Morrison has been reassigned to AHL Coachella Valley. Lindgren left Seattle’s October 6 game against the Vegas Golden Knights with an upper-body injury and was placed on IR two days later. At the time, he was given a four-to-six-week recovery window and returns after roughly five and a half weeks, just in time for Saturday’s Global Series finale against the Carolina Hurricanes in Helsinki. The former second-round pick had no points and a +3 rating through Seattle’s first four games before the injury. In the 13 games he has missed, the Kraken went 7-5-1 over that stretch to reach 9-7-1 overall. While the team overall has held their own over the last month, sitting just two points back of the third spot in the Pacific, his return could help steady a Seattle defense that has struggled without him. The Kraken entered the Global Series 29th in goals allowed per game and 31st on the penalty kill. Lindgren is in the second year of the four-year, $18MM contract he signed in free agency in July 2025. Morrison was called up on November 8 as extra forward depth for the trip to Finland. With only one game left before the Kraken head home, he goes back to the Firebirds, where he has three goals and nine points in 12 games this season. The 24-year-old led Coachella Valley with 61 points in 68 games last year. His only NHL experience is four games in 2023-24, and he is still looking for his first NHL point.

items.summary: Roman Josi scored the deciding goal in the fourth round of a shootout as the Nashville Predators beat the Vegas Golden Knights 3-2 Friday night for their seventh straight win.
items.body: LAS VEGAS — Roman Josi scored the deciding goal in the fourth round of a shootout as the Nashville Predators beat the Vegas Golden Knights 3-2 Friday night for their seventh straight win. Ryan O’Reilly scored twice for the Predators. Juuse Saros made 40 saves. Victor Olofsson and Rasmus Andersson scored for Vegas, which had its four-game winning streak snapped. Adin Hill stopped 30 shots. Trevor Connelly gave Vegas the early advantage in the shootout, but Filip Forsberg kept Nashville alive with a third-round goal. After Saros denied Jack Eichel, Josi converted to complete the comeback. Braeden Bowman and Mitch Marner also missed for Vegas. Steven Stamkos and O’Reilly were unsuccessful for Nashville. Olofsson nearly ended the game early in overtime, but his shot rang off the post. The Golden Knights extended their point streak to six games despite the loss. Nashville won its fourth consecutive road game. Olofsson continued his productive return from injury with his sixth goal in eight appearances this season. He had a goal and two assists in Wednesday’s 5-3 victory over Utah and entered Friday with four points in three games since returning Nov. 5 at Detroit. Andersson scored his third goal of the season, while O’Reilly increased his total to nine. Nashville entered with strong goaltending throughout its winning streak. Saros and Justus Annunen combined for a 1.63 goals-against average and .942 save percentage over the previous six victories, allowing 10 goals. Saros was named the NHL’s third star of the week Monday after stopping 53 of 55 shots across two wins. The Predators entered the night with the NHL’s second-ranked penalty kill, erasing 89.5 per cent of opponents’ power plays, and stopped Vegas on its only power-play opportunity.

Staggering through a hectic and historically bad first quarter of the National Hockey League season, the Canucks finally got a chance to rest and practise. But only the resting part was evident Friday against the New York Rangers. The Canucks rested in the second period, surrendering as many goals as they generated shots (four) and were embarrassed again in a 5-1 loss, their 17th defeat in 18 games since Oct. 3 and their eighth straight loss at Rogers Arena. It sounds impossible that in the Year 2026, with the experienced National Hockey League players the Canucks have kept on their roster for the start of the Great Rebuild, the team could be this bad. But despite underlying numbers and common sense that suggest Vancouver should have another three or four wins, they actually are this bad — and will continue to be this bad — as long as they go missing for large swaths of games. “The story of the second (period) was just our unwillingness or inability to stick to the script,” Canucks head coach Manny Malhotra said. “Our first period was probably the best we've looked in a long time, just in terms of everything structurally. items.summary: Brock Boeser has cemented his place in Vancouver Canucks history with a major milestone.
items.body: Brock Boeser has cemented his place in Vancouver Canucks history with a major milestone. The veteran forward collected his 500th point in a Canucks uniform on Friday, becoming just the eighth player in franchise history to do so. Boeser's milestone point came with an assist on a first-period goal by Elias Pettersson. "It means a lot," Boeser told Sportsnet's Dan Murphy during the first intermission. "I've been here a long time and anytime you can get a milestone like that it means the world, and just happy to do it with these guys." The Canucks drafted Boeser in the first round, 23rd overall, of the 2015 NHL Draft, and he is the longest-tenured player on the team. The 29-year-old has skated in 650 games over his 11-year career, collecting 233 goals and 267 assists. The other players to score 500 points with the Canucks are Henrik Sedin (1,070), Daniel Sedin (1,041), Markus Naslund (756), Trevor Linden (733), Stan Smyl (673), Thomas Gradin (550) and Pettersson (529).

While he largely did just that, it wasn’t enough to keep his roster spot; the team announced today that the netminder has been sent back to AHL San Diego. The 33-year-old signed a one-year, $1.1MM contract back in the summer and was expected to have a chance to battle for the backup job in training camp. However, with no appreciable improvement between the pipes despite their recent run, the decision was made to return Brossoit to the minors for now. "The Great One" is the only player in NHL history to eclipse 200 points in a season, doing so four times in a five-year span — last done in 1985-86 — but the Oilers' current superstar is making quite the case to join Gretzky's exclusive group. McDavid entered Friday with 49 points (11 goals, 38 assists) through the first 20 games of the season, putting him on pace to finish the regular season with 206 points — which would surpass Gretzky's 205 (1983-84) for fourth-most in NHL history. I can’t think of one,” five-time Stanley Cup champ with the Oilers and Hall of Famer Jari Kurri told NHL.com . “He might slow down here and there, but he might come back again. It’s a long season and it’s a lot of games, a lot of travel, but hopefully he stays healthy. “And, sure, if he stays healthy and keeps playing like that, I’m sure he will.” Esa Tikkanen, who also played alongside Gretzky, echoed those sentiments: “When the games come later in the season, they’ll be tougher and it’s going to be harder and harder all the time. I think he has a good chance, but there are still 60 games left. items.title: Report: NHL expected to extend Texas expansion evaluation process
items.body: The NHL doesn't appear ready to finalize expansion plans to Texas just yet. Jennifer Streeter of PuckPedia reports that, according to multiple sources "closely connected to expansion efforts," the NHL is expected to extend the evaluation process to determine whether it will award an expansion franchise to a group led by Texas billionaire Dan Friedkin. The NHL and The Friedkin Group entered a six-month exploratory process in June that was designed to look into the viability of adding a 33rd franchise to Houston or Austin, Texas. That process was due to be completed before the end of the year and an update is expected at the NHL's next Board of Governors meeting in early December. If awarded, the new Texas franchise would come with a $3.5 billion price tag. Of that, $1.5 billion would be earmarked to build a new arena and the other $2 billion paid to the NHL as an expansion fee. Speaking at the last Board of Governors meetings in September, NHL commissioner Gary Bettman said the league was in no rush to expand and cautioned that any transaction of this size doesn't happen overnight. “We're not under any time constraint,” Bettman said. “This isn't a situation where we said, 'We're going to expand by X date, get your applications in.’ We're dealing with unsolicited — but we're grateful to have them — expressions of interest. And it'll sort itself out on whatever timetable makes sense to everybody." The NHL has twice expanded in the last decade — to Las Vegas in 2017 and Seattle in 2021 — and now has 32 franchises. The awarding of an expansion franchise requires a three-fourths majority of support in a vote of the league's 32 governors.

items.body: “There was a stat a couple of years ago, where he had less games with no points (12), than he had games with three or more points (13). Like, I don’t get that many points in practice. In a season.” — Oilers defenceman Connor Murphy. TORONTO — There will never be another Wayne Gretzky, hockey’s all-time leading scorer who had more career assists (1,963) than second place Jaromir Jagr has career points (1,921). But as Connor McDavid rolls into Toronto for a Saturday night game against the Toronto Maple Leafs , a 20-game, season-opening points streak in tow, there’s definitely a Gretzkian vibe around McDavid. He is, as Gretzky was, the Toronto-area kid who landed in Alberta’s capital, and the envy of Leafs Nation. And as he readies himself to set a new personal mark by extending his points streak to 21 games on Saturday (Sportsnet, Sportsnet+, 7 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. ABT), like almost any new milestone that McDavid can imagine, it inevitably pales to something Gretzky once did. In this case it was Gretzky’s 51-game points streak in the 1983-84 season in which Gretzky averaged exactly three points per game. That season, Gretzky’s first pointless game came on Jan. 27, at home against New Jersey, his shoulder injured and his spirit waning just five games short of Joe DiMaggio’s iconic 56-game hitting streak in baseball. “We knew he was always going to take care of business, that he was always going to get his chances,” said Paul Coffey, the Evan Bouchard to Gretzky, back in the day. “We never had to say. ‘Okay, let's get Gretz a point tonight.’ Never. But I tell you, if he gives it to you, you’d better (expletive) finish.” Today, the eldest Oiler — 1990-born Mattias Ekholm — came into this world two years after Gretzky’s last Stanley Cup. The Great One never played in the 2000’s.

items.title: Five thoughts about the NHL at the quarter mark
items.summary: As teams hit Game 21 of their NHL schedules, Justin Bourne has gained real clarity on a number of pre-season questions.
items.body: TORONTO — As teams hit Game 21 of their NHL schedules — a nice, clean quarter-mark divider in an 84-game schedule — we’ve gained real clarity on a number of pre-season questions. I’ve got five thoughts as we hit a schedule milestone, so let’s not waste time: If someone is going to tear down a house and rebuild it, these things are not Step A, then Step B. It’s Step A, and then Steps B all the way through Z. The rebuild takes months, while the teardown takes days. That seems relevant for all the teams that have recently been praised for their savvy teardowns, but watching Chicago stuck in the mud has been a real reminder about the challenge that comes with the other steps. Vancouver is still doing demo work, but San Jose has started to erect walls, and it might not be the mansion they hoped. Detroit appears to be rebuilding using sticks and mud, and it’s not looking great nearly a decade into turning things around. As the league gets bigger, and the elite-talent spread gets thinner, it’s a reminder that things have to go horribly wrong with “retool” attempts before a team should commit itself to starting over. It’s hard to get elite guys, so if you’ve got a couple, it’s probably worth trying to do renovations for a while before you bring the whole structure down. Real Kyper and Bourne Nick Kypreos and Justin Bourne talk all things hockey with some of the biggest names in the game. items.title: Canucks defenceman Tom Willander available to play vs. Rangers
items.body: Defenceman Tom Willander could be back in the lineup when his Vancouver Canucks host the New York Rangers on Friday. Head coach Manny Malhotra says the 21-year-old Swedish blueliner will be available after missing the last four games with a lower-body injury. Willander has three goals over 16 games for the Canucks (3-16-1) this season and is averaging 20:25 in ice time. Malhotra also says centre Filip Chytil is "progressing" from a shoulder injury and will be evaluated after Friday's morning skate. Chytil has been out since Oct. 29 when he was sent into the boards via a hard hit from San Jose Sharks defenceman Darnell Nurse. He was place on injured reserve the following day. The 27-year-old Czech forward has two assists on the season after missing the first eight games with an upper-body injury he picked up in pre-season play.

items.title: Stars’ Lian Bichsel out at least two weeks with lower-body injury
items.summary: Bichsel suffered an injury during Thursday night’s game against the Winnipeg Jets.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images One of the biggest players in the league (literally) is going to miss some time. When speaking to the media on Friday, Dallas Stars head coach Glen Gulutzan announced that defenseman Lian Bichsel is going to miss the next two weeks due to a lower-body injury. Gulutzan acknowledged that the Swiss blueliner is officially listed as week-to-week. Gulutzan also said that defender Miro Heiskanen won’t be in the lineup on Saturday, when the Stars host the Buffalo Sabres . However, the Finnish star isn’t be ruled out for Sunday’s matchup with the Florida Panthers. Bichsel suffered the injury during Thursday night’s clash with the Winnipeg Jets. Early in the first period, Jets forward Mark Scheifele became entangled with Stars blueliner Esa Lindell. As the two started falling to the ice, Bichsel, also looking to throw a hit on Scheifele, was tripped up, apparently bending his left ankle in an awkward fashion. Bichsel lay on the ice for several minutes before being helped off the ice by his teammates and training staff. The team later revealed that the 6-foot-7 rearguard wouldn’t be returning to the contest. He registered just 1:14 of ice time across two shifts. Bichsel had appeared in each of the first 18 games of Dallas’ 2026-27 season. He has yet to find the back of the net this year, but he did post an assist in a win over the New York Islanders on Oct. 25. He has a plus/minus of -4 while averaging 15:29 of ice time per game. The Olten native is in the final season of his three-year, entry-level contract. The deal carries an AAV of $1,418,333. The Stars (10-6-2) sit fourth in the Central Division, holding the first Wild Card spot in the Western Conference.
